item.title: 10 children and 2 caregivers: Inside Elon Musk's $600 million failed school experiment
item.description: Elon Musk's ambitious vision to revolutionize education with interactive, game-like learning has faced significant hurdles. His elementary school, Ad Astra, initially envisioned for hundreds, operates as a small childcare facility in Texas. Despite substantial funding, Musk's educational ventures have seen closures and shifts online, suggesting a challenging path for his entrepreneurial endeavors in this sector. Read more here!
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘First casualty of the fusion wars’: Killing of MIT’s top nuclear scientist Nuno Loureiro sparks online speculation
item.description: Leading nuclear fusion scientist Nuno Loureiro was tragically killed at his Massachusetts home, sparking widespread online speculation. While authorities investigate the homicide with no suspects identified, theories link his death to the global race for fusion energy. Loureiro, director of MIT's Plasma Science and Fusion Center, was a respected figure in the field.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Adin Ross instantly bans Mizkif from his Kick chat during livestream
item.description: Streamer Adin Ross reignited his feud with Mizkif by instantly banning him from his Kick chat. Ross publicly mocked Mizkif's engagement numbers, while Mizkif later responded on X, questioning Ross's perceived double standards regarding serious allegations. This incident highlights the ongoing tension between the two creators, suggesting further public clashes are likely.

item.title: Mike Liaory accident goes viral after Kick stream shows red light crash in Los Angeles traffic
item.description: Live streamer Mike Liaory's dangerous stunt of running a red light while broadcasting on Kick led to a serious car crash in Los Angeles. The incident, captured on video, shows his vehicle colliding with another at a busy intersection. The footage has sparked widespread debate about the risks of streaming while driving.

item.title: “Ain’t no way”: Nina Lin addresses Twitch permaban rumors after viral Target stream
item.description: Streamer Nina Lin has denied claims of a permanent Twitch ban following her viral Target livestream. While her channel displays a message often associated with indefinite suspensions, Lin insists the rumors are false and plans to return to the platform. This follows previous bans related to theft and resurfaced clips, leaving her future on Twitch uncertain.

item.title: First American Pope appoints Bishop Ronald Hicks as New York’s next archbishop
item.description: Pope Leo XIV has appointed Bishop Ronald Hicks of Joliet as the next Archbishop of New York, replacing Cardinal Timothy Dolan. A Chicago native with deep ties to Latin America and immigrant advocacy, Hicks inherits leadership of one of the US Church’s largest archdioceses, alongside oversight of a $300 million abuse settlement fund and a shifting political landscape.

item.title: Two Haitian immigrants charged in $7 million SNAP fraud scheme
item.description: Two Haitian immigrants face federal charges in Boston for allegedly orchestrating a $7 million SNAP benefit fraud scheme. Prosecutors claim they exchanged food stamps for cash at two tiny stores, Jesula Variety Store and Saul Maché Mixé Store, over 20 months. The case highlights potential weaknesses in SNAP retailer oversight, not widespread recipient fraud.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 'Absolutely': Trump says he would denaturalize 100-200 people per month in 2026 if...
item.description: Immigration field officers have been asked to report 100-200 denaturalization cases per month in 2026 in a new and aggressive phase of Trump's crackdown. Denaturalization or the process in which a US citizen loses citizenship is rare. But Trump confirmed that if he has the power to take away people's citizenship, he would absolutely proceed with it.

item.title: “Completely ignorant”: Inside the ‘ball and gun’ gamer debate and why The Black Hokage is critical of the modern gaming culture at large
item.description: The term “ball and gun gamer,” coined by Twitch streamer The Black Hokage, describes players who stick mainly to sports and shooter games while dismissing other genres. He stresses the label is not about casual enjoyment, but about judging games without experience. His comments went viral for calling out narrow perspectives in gaming culture.

item.title: Indian-origin techie at centre of anti-India hate hackathon says he has landed his dream job at xAI
item.description: Vineeth Sendilraj, a Georgia Tech student, has joined Elon Musk's AI company xAI. This move follows his viral moment at the xAI hackathon. His image was widely shared, leading to a controversy that resulted in another executive's dismissal. Sendilraj's team won the hackathon, securing his position as an engineer. He is known for his AI and high-performance systems projects.

item.title: Why did CDawgVA fire shots at SoLLUMINATI? YouTuber faces major backlash after his viral comments on Ironmouse
item.description: Streamer CDawgVA has publicly slammed SoLLUMINATI after the latter made remarks about Ironmouse's VTuber identity and her personal life. SoLLUMINATI questioned the difference between Ironmouse's online persona and her real self, unaware of her health condition. CDawgVA criticized this lack of basic knowledge, getting praise from fans who urged creators to educate themselves before commenting on sensitive topics.
